title: Infant and Toddler Kit
description: Use this list to pack emergency supplies for babies and young children, based on CDC's infant feeding in emergencies checklist.

sources.title: Emergency List for Families With Infants and Young Children
Facts About Infant Feeding During Emergencies

items.text: Formula-fed babies: ready-to-feed formula in single-serving bottles or cans - the safest choice because it needs no water or mixing
Check every month that you have several days of formula at your baby's current amount, and replace any near expiration
Powdered formula backup only with its kit: bottled water for mixing, liquid measuring cup, lidded mixing container, bottles, and nipples
Safe drinking water such as sealed bottled water
Breastfeeding: disposable nursing pads (1-2 boxes)
Pumping: manual breast pump for outages, milk storage bags, and a small cooler with ice packs; spare pump parts, cords, and batteries
Disposable cups, dishes, feeding spoons, and bibs - use them if you cannot wash reusable items with safe water
Cleaning kit for bottles and pump parts: wash basin, scrub brush, dish soap, and drying bag in a lidded container
At least one large pack of diapers and two packs of baby wipes
Diaper rash cream, baby wash, and lotion
Gallon-size zip bags for dirty diapers and clothes
Infant thermometer and an infant pain and fever reliever with its measuring device (follow the label)
Child's medical records and vaccination record
Nonperishable baby food and snacks right for your child's age
Baby carrier (sling, wrap, or front or back carrier) so your hands are free when evacuating
Extra clothes and at least two extra blankets
Portable crib or travel bed for safe sleep
Burp cloths and at least two pacifiers if used
Bulb syringe
Tape and a marker for labeling bottles and supplies
Camp stove, fuel, and pot for boiling water - used outdoors only
Comfort toy and a few small activities for toddlers
Never water down formula to stretch it - mix exactly as the label says with safe water, use it within 2 hours, and ask a shelter or health worker for help if supplies run low
